title: A group's daily cap counts no spend of a finished bench job, so it bounds only the budgets of jobs alive together
goal: a finished paid job's record keeps the USD it spent (spent_usd, written by the executor at its end from the job's own spend rows), kj_store.finished_spend sums spent_usd of the finished jobs of the group submitted on the UTC day, whether or not the subject is a backlog item, and the daily cap check reads that sum and the live budgets inside one transaction

run: import sys,time; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import kj_store; t=time.time(); r=[{'subject':'s1','state':'succeeded','submitted_ts':t,'placement':{'decided_by':'corp'},'spent_usd':4.5}]; v=kj_store.finished_spend('.', r, 'corp', t); assert v==4.5, v

the spend_usd rows of benchmarks.csv for the job's scenario

gates.answer: the spend line benchmarks.py prints for each scenario that paid, in the job's output

options: keep it, unread, as the repro's call shape has it
gates.recommendation: keep it, unread, as the repro's call shape has it
gates.answer: keep it, unread, as the repro's call shape has it

gates.question: Which ends of a job write its spent_usd, and what does an attempt add?

only a succeeded or failed end, the last attempt replacing the figure
